searchText: It could be quite outdated question, but why eth2.0 plan to use VDF instead of VRF? If I had to give an argument, I'd say one of the reasons is that VRF is secure *after* selection, i.e. needs checking. Randao and Randao + VDF are secure ahead of time. You know the number will be random without checking. In Eth where there will potentially be hundreds of thousands of people validating, it would be incredibly difficult to check all the VRF rolls, but with VDF there's only one thing to check against the incoming blocks. So VRF, you get blocks, then check them along with the proof submitted by the validator. With VDF, blocks get checked against the random roll that's common for everyone. Additional proof per block not needed. <@291925846556540928> okay I've tried a write-up that focuses on the technical issue rather than assign motive to any parties. Please read https://hackmd.io/bCZjQnOyRBqxyHKxKnTz0Q?view Also, I've put together a PR with a test that fails with the current contract but succeeds with the amended contract (also in the PR): https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/pull/1506 Hopefully either the text or the test (or both in conjunction) should be enough to highlight the issue and explain its fix. Note MrChico noted on the PR that someone could still front-run the transaction, but this will cost them a minimum of 1 Ether each time and the patch still ensures that funds cannot be stolen <@387303511626350593> Randao + VDF doesn’t need additional proof, so it’s more efficient than VRF right? What about randomness itself? I think it’s quite hard to set the public input x in VRFVAL(sk, x). So it could be vulnerable if we don’t choose x properly. <@494491139085172736> Wrong channel. It's an Ethereum 2.0 discord. lmao oh ye <@422694466428600330> not qualified to speak on efficiency, wish I knew. Re x I only know how it was implemented in Polkadot and that works rather well: https://youtu.be/ZVWqcxe-KKY
